<reason>B built the cleaner comparative path: the documented, current harms of news deserts versus a capture risk A never evidenced. A landed a real methodological hit (news-desert studies measure dead private papers, not firewalled subsidies) and offered an original "credential/alibi" mechanism, but B answered it with the active-ingredient/wrapper argument and the status-quo-bias reframe, then turned A's own answer to "name one captured newsroom" — capture is invisible — into the debate's decisive concession: an unfalsifiable harm that proves too much, since invisible editorial capture describes private ownership equally. On a "more than" motion, A's risk stayed hypothetical while B's harms stayed measured, and B's counterfactual framing (flawed watchdog vs empty chair) was never dislodged. Both sides followed the Q/A format cleanly; A actually had the last word each round but used closings largely to restate rather than resolve.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's sequence from Q1 ("name one captured firewalled newsroom") through the closing: when A answered that capture is invisible ("the series that never starts"), B converted it into a double bind — the harm is unobservable assertion, and the same invisible-capture logic disqualifies every private newsroom too, defaulting to the empty chair A concedes is ugly. A's "funder identity is the whole point" reply asserted the distinction without rebuilding the weighing.</best_rebuttal>
